name: track_points
description: Follow anchor points through the footage under one item (normally an overlay), for shapes pinned to the footage: one position per frame for each anchor. Coordinates are design-canvas pixels (the overlay's coordinates): 1080 on the short edge with the aspect of settings.resolution, whatever the export resolution, so 1920x1080 for any 16:9 project. The footage is the composite glass_plate draws for the item's range (the video and image tracks, never overlays or captions, every transform and speed applied), tracked at half the design canvas and scaled back. Frame n is the screen frame under the overlay's frame n, round(start * fps) + n, over round(end * fps) - round(start * fps) frames. Each anchor's frame-0 patch is matched in every frame (normalized cross correlation within the search radius around the last position plus the last velocity, refined to subpixel), never frame to frame and never a global shift. minScore is each anchor's lowest match score: 1 is a perfect match. Below 0.3 the match is not the patch (covered, changed, or never distinct): the point coasts on its last trusted motion, slowing to a stop, keeps searching there, and picks the patch up again at the first match of 0.3 or more that peaks inside the search. lostFrames counts those frames per anchor. A minScore under 0.3, or any lostFrames, means move the anchor to detail that stays visible and distinct over the item; from 0.3 to about 0.5 the patch is faint and the track can slip onto look-alike texture (foliage, water), so check it on a frame. -9 means its patch left the frame for some frames: there the point coasted on its last velocity (the motion before it left). Near an edge the search is moved inside the frame, so a point that stops near an edge stays on it, and a patch that comes back into the frame at up to the search radius per frame is found again, its motion restarting from 0. A patch that stops exactly flush with the frame edge is read as leaving and coasts away. Needs numpy (the rvm extra).

input.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json

output.description: { tracks: { <id>: [[x, y] per frame] } in design-canvas px, 2 decimals; minScore: { <id>: n }; lostFrames: { <id>: frames the point coasted inside the frame without a trusted match }; fps; frames; scale: working px per design px (0.5); workingSize: [w, h]; canvas: [w, h] of the design canvas }

params.name: project
params.description: The project id, its folder, or the absolute path of its project.json

params.name: item
params.description: Id of the item the tracks are for, normally the overlay item. Its start and end set the range. Any item in the project is accepted; an unknown id is an error.

params.name: anchors
params.description: A string: the anchors as JSON text, e.g. '[{"id": "tile1", "x": 600, "y": 430}]', or the path of a .json file holding that array. Pass the JSON as a string, not as an array value. Each anchor is a point on visible detail in the item's first frame, in design-canvas pixels. Ids are unique and name the tracks. An anchor whose patch does not fit inside the frame, or sits on a flat patch, is refused by id.

params.name: patch
params.description: Side of the square patch matched around each anchor, in design-canvas px.

params.name: search
params.description: Search radius around the predicted position (the last position plus the last per-frame motion), in working px, half the design canvas: 7 finds the patch when its per-frame motion jumps by up to 14 design px from one frame to the next; the prediction follows a change of motion by at most half the radius (7 design px) a frame.

params.name: smooth
params.description: ma5: a centred 5-frame moving average whose window shrinks symmetrically at the ends (the first and last frames raw, the second and second-to-last over 3), so motion at the ends keeps no lag. quad: a quadratic fit per axis over the range, which hides sway. none: the raw track.
